features: Existing net/HTTP performance producers construct privately branded PerformanceNodeEntry instances inheriting from the global PerformanceEntry. Measured start/duration and merged request/response details are preserved.

Entries expose validated read-only getters, fresh toJSON objects retaining detail identity, inherited class identity and the Node-compatible Object tag. Ordinary TCP and HTTP controls pass under Node and built Home.
limitations: Borrowed native PerformanceEntry base methods, global/native constructor interactions, inspection, additional producers and full performance/platform behavior remain open under #869/#873. The new subclass does not establish complete native base interoperability.

The nine original selected files retain 62 passes, three process checks, one failure/failed file (#874), 40 filtered cases and zero skips/TODOs. Assertions and snapshots are unchanged; full suite parity remains unproven.

Initial Home identity failure and Node tag expectation correction are retained. The first build began before the tag correction; final verification uses the corrected recovery build. Corrected-build disk admission refusal and terminal-derived cleanup are retained. Pickier reports zero errors and three existing warnings.

Corpus integration remains open in #876; HTTPS receiver/lifecycle in #875/#532. Excluded constructor/Deno regressions were not rerun. #872, full Bun suite and Release/ASAN/all-platform verification remain open under #66.
